extracted.intended_audience: high-school students and coaches preparing for national/regional mathematics competitions (math olympiads)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of numbered mathematical problems from regional/national olympiad competitions (geometry, combinatorics, number theory, inequalities, games, constructions) intended to be solved and proved by contestants. Each item specifies a task statement and any constraints or subparts.

rubrics_metrics.description: Given positive numbers a,b,c,d. Prove that the set of inequalities a+b<c+d; (a+b)(c+d)<ab+cd; (a+b)cd<ab(c+d) contain at least one wrong.
For what minimal natural a the polynomial ax^2 + bx + c with the integer c and b has two different positive roots both less than one.
Given natural n. Consider all the fractions 1/(pq), where p and q are relatively prime; 0<p<q<=n ; p+q>n. Prove that the sum of all such fractions equals to 1/2.

Given n points in the three dimensional space such, that the arbitrary triangle with the vertices in three of those points contains an angle greater than 120 degrees. Prove that You can rearrange them to make a polyline (unclosed) with all the angles between the sequent links greater than 120 degrees.
Find four different three-digit decimal numbers starting with the same digit, such that their sum is divisible by three of them.

Every city in the certain state is connected by airlines with no more than with three other ones, but one can get from every city to every other city changing a plane once only or directly. What is the maximal possible number of the cities?

rubrics_metrics.name: 124a
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pentagon with all equal sides. a) Prove that there exist such a point on the maximal diagonal, that every side is seen from it inside a right angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarification: 'side AB is seen from the point C inside an arbitrary angle that is greater or equal than angle ACB.'

rubrics_metrics.name: 124b
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pentagon with all equal sides. b) Prove that the circles build on its sides as on the diameters cannot cover the pentagon entirely.

Given an equation x^3 + ?x^2 + ?x + ? = 0. First player substitutes an integer on the place of one of the interrogative marks, then the second with one of the two remained marks, and, finally, the first puts the integer instead of the last mark. Explain how can the first provide the existence of three integer roots in the obtained equation. (The roots may coincide.)

20 football teams participate in the championship. What minimal number of the games should be played to provide the property: from the three arbitrary teams we can find at least one pair that have already met in the championship.
Let h_k be an apothem of the right k-angle inscribed into a circle with radius R. Prove that (n + 1) h_{n+1} - n h_n > R.
Prove that for the arbitrary positive a1, a2, ..., an the following inequality is held: a1/(a2+a3) + a2/(a3+a4) + ... + a_{n-1}/(a_n+a1) + a_n/(a1+a2) > -n/4.

Given a circle, its diameter [AB] and a point C on it. Build (with the help of compasses and ruler) two points X and Y, that are symmetric with respect to (AB) line, such that (YC) is orthogonal to (XA).
The product of three positive numbers equals to one, their sum is strictly greater than the sum of the inverse numbers. Prove that one and only one of them is greater than one.
How many sides of the convex polygon can equal its longest diagonal?
The digits of the 17-digit number are rearranged in the reverse order. Prove that at least one digit of the sum of the new and the initial number is even.

rubrics_metrics.name: 133a
rubrics_metrics.description: A castle is equilateral triangle with the side of 100 metres. It is divided onto 100 triangle rooms. Each wall between the rooms is 10 metres long and contain one door. You are inside and are allowed to pass through every door not more than once. Prove that You can visit not more than 91 rooms (not exiting the castle).

rubrics_metrics.name: 133b
rubrics_metrics.description: Every side of the triangle is divided onto k parts by the lines parallel to the sides. And the triangle is divided onto k^2 small triangles. Let us call the 'chain' such a sequence of triangles, that every triangle in it is included only once, and the consecutive triangles have the common side. What is the greatest possible number of the triangles in the chain?
Given five segments. It is possible to build a triangle of every subset of three of them. Prove that at least one of those triangles is acute-angled.
The bisector [AD], the median [BM] and the height [CH] of the acute-angled triangle ABC intersect in one point. Prove that the angle BAC is greater than 45 degrees.
Given five n-digit binary numbers. For each two numbers their digits coincide exactly on m places. There is no place with the common digit for all the five numbers. Prove that 2/5 <= m/n <= 3/5.
Prove that from every set of 200 integers You can choose a subset of 100 with the total sum divisible by 100.

Given triangle ABC, middle M of the side [BC], the centre O of the inscribed circle. The line (MO) crosses the height AH in the point E. Prove that the distance |AE| equals the inscribed circle radius.

Prove that for every natural number k there exists an infinite set of such natural numbers t, that the decimal notation of t does not contain zeroes and the sums of the digits of the numbers t and kt are equal.
Two equal rectangles are intersecting in 8 points. Prove that the common part area is greater than the half of the rectangle's area.
All the 5-digit numbers from 11111 to 99999 are written on the cards. Those cards lies in a line in an arbitrary order. Prove that the resulting 444445-digit number is not a power of two.

All natural numbers containing not more than n digits are divided onto two groups. The first contains the numbers with the even sum of the digits, the second -- with the odd sum. Prove that if 0<k<n than the sum of the k-th powers of the numbers in the first group equals to the sum of the k-th powers of the numbers in the second group.

The vertices of the right n-angle are marked with some colours (each vertex -- with one colour) in such a way, that the vertices of one colour represent the right polygon. Prove that there are two equal ones among the smaller polygons.
Prove that for every natural n there exists a number, containing only digits '1' and '2' in its decimal notation, that is divisible by 2^n (n-th power of two).

rubrics_metrics.name: 145a
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a triangle A1A2A3 and the points B1 and D2 on the side [A1A2], B2 and D3 on the side [A2A3], B3 and D1 on the side [A3A1]. If You build parallelograms A1B1C1D1, A2B2C2D2 and A3B3C3D3, the lines (A1C1), (A2C2) and (A3C3), will cross in one point O. Prove that if |A1B1| = |A2D2| and |A2B2| = |A3D3|, than |A3B3| = |A1D1|.

rubrics_metrics.name: 145b
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a convex polygon A1A2...An and the points B1 and D2 on the side [A1A2], B2 and D3 on the side [A2A3], ..., Bn and D1 on the side [AnA1]. If You build parallelograms A1B1C1D1, A2B2C2D2, ..., AnBnCnDn, the lines (A1C1), (A2C2), ..., (AnCn), will cross in one point O. Prove that |A1B1|*|A2B2|*...*|AnBn| = |A1D1|*|A2D2|*...*|AnDn|.

rubrics_metrics.name: 146a
rubrics_metrics.description: A game for two. The first player writes two rows of ten numbers each, the second under the first. He should provide the following property: if number b is written under a, and d -- under c, then a + d = b + c. The second player has to determine all the numbers. He is allowed to ask the questions like 'What number is written in the x place in the y row?' What is the minimal number of the questions asked by the second player before he finds out all the numbers?

rubrics_metrics.name: 146b
rubrics_metrics.description: There was a table m x n on the blackboard with the property: if You chose two rows and two columns, then the sum of the numbers in the two opposite vertices of the rectangles formed by those lines equals the sum of the numbers in two another vertices. Some of the numbers are cleaned, but it is still possible to restore all the table. What is the minimal possible number of the remaining numbers?

Given a unit square and some circles inside. Radius of each circle is less than 0.001, and there is no couple of points belonging to the different circles with the distance between them 0.001 exactly. Prove that the area, covered by the circles is not greater than 0.34.

The volumes of the water contained in each of three big enough containers are integers. You are allowed only to relocate some times from one container to another the same volume of the water, that the destination already contains. Prove that You are able to discharge one of the containers.

Prove that if the numbers p1, p2, q1, q2 satisfy the condition (q1 - q2)^2 + (p1 - p2)(p1 q2 - p2 q1) < 0, then the quadratic polynomials x^2 + p1 x + q1 and x^2 + p2 x + q2 have real roots, and between the roots of each there is a root of another one.
The projections of the body on two planes are circles. Prove that they have the same radius.

Some numbers are written along the ring. If inequality (a-d)(b-c) < 0 is held for the four arbitrary numbers in sequence a,b,c,d, You have to change the numbers b and c places. Prove that You will have to do this operation finite number of times.

rubrics_metrics.name: 152a
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that the line dividing the triangle onto two polygons with equal perimeters and equal areas passes through the centre of the inscribed circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: 152b
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the same statement for the arbitrary polygon circumscribed around a circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: 152c
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that all the lines halving its perimeter and area simultaneously, intersect in one point.
Given 25 different positive numbers. Prove that You can choose two of them such, that none of the other numbers equals neither to the sum nor to the difference between the chosen numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 154a
rubrics_metrics.description: The vertex A1 of the regular 12-gon A1A2...A12 is marked with '-' and all the rest -- with '+'. You are allowed to change the sign simultaneously in the 6 vertices in succession. Prove that is impossible to obtain dodecagon with A2 marked with '-' and the rest of the vertices -- with '+'.

rubrics_metrics.name: 154b
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the same statement if it is allowed to change the signs not in six, but in four vertices in succession.

rubrics_metrics.name: 154c
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the same statement if it is allowed to change the signs in three vertices in succession.

N unit squares on the infinite sheet of cross-lined paper are painted black. Prove that You can cut out a finite number of square pieces and satisfy two conditions: all the black squares are contained in those pieces; the area of black squares is not less than 1/5 and not greater than 4/5 of every piece area.

rubrics_metrics.name: 156a
rubrics_metrics.description: A cube with the edge of length n is divided onto n^3 unit ones. Let us choose some of them and draw three lines parallel to the edges through their centres. What is the least possible number of the chosen small cubes necessary to make those lines cross all the smaller cubes? Find the answer for small n (n = 2,3,4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 156b
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to find the answer for n = 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: 156c
rubrics_metrics.description: If You can not solve the general problem, try to estimate that value from the upper and lower side.

rubrics_metrics.name: 156d
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformulation: Consider all the triples (x1,x2,x3), where xi in {1,...,n}. What is the minimal number of the triples necessary to provide the property: for each of the triples there exist the chosen one, that differs only in one coordinate. Try to find the answer for more than three coordinates, e.g., four.

rubrics_metrics.name: 157a
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the function f(x,y) = x^2 + xy + y^2. Prove that for every point (x,y) there exist integers (m,n), that f((x-m),(y-n)) <= 1/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: 157b
rubrics_metrics.description: Let g(x,y) be the least possible value of f((x-m),(y-n)) for all integers m,n. Prove that in fact g(x,y) <= 1/3. Find all the points (x,y), where g(x,y)=1/3.

rubrics_metrics.name: 157c
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider function f_a(x,y) = x^2 + axy + y^2 (0 <= a <= 2). Find any c such that g_a(x,y) <= c. Try to obtain the closest estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158a
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to build the universal scheme for 4 inputs and 4 outputs, that can provide all of 24 possible connections (switch network problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: switching elements as shown in figure; universal schemes enable all permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158b
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the minimal number of the element switches for such a scheme?

rubrics_metrics.name: 158c
rubrics_metrics.description: Given scheme with 8 inputs/outputs where A and B are 4-universal, prove that it is 8-universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes figure c and asks to prove 8-universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: 158d
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the upper and lower bound for the number of the element switches in the n-universal scheme.

Given a rectangle ABCD, points M -- the middle of [AD] side, N -- the middle of [BC] side. Let P be a point on the continuation of the [DC] segment over the point D. Let Q be the intersection of lines PM and AC. Prove that the angles QNM and MNP are equal.
Given 50 segments on the line. Prove that one of the following statements is valid: 1) Some 8 segments have the common point. 2) Some 8 segments do not intersect each other.
Find the maximal x such that the expression 4/27 + 4/1000 + 4/x is an exact square.

rubrics_metrics.name: 162a
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a,n,m be natural numbers, a > 1. Prove that if (a^m + 1) is divisible by (a^n + 1) then m is divisible by n.

rubrics_metrics.name: 162b
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a,b,n,m be natural numbers, a>1, a and b are relatively prime. Prove that if (a^m + b^m) is divisible by (a^n + b^n) then m is divisible by n.
Triangle table: put natural number a>1 in the top; then under number k from the left write k^2, from the right (k+1). Prove that all the numbers on each particular line are different.
Given several squares with the total area 1. Prove that You can place them in a square of area 2 without any intersections.

Let O be intersection of diagonals of convex quadrilateral ABCD. Prove that the line through the intersection points of medians of triangles AOB and COD is orthogonal to the line through intersection points of altitudes of BOC and AOD.
Each of the 9 straight lines divides the given square into two quadrangles with areas related as 2:3. Prove that there exist three of them intersecting in one point.
The 7-gon A1...A7 is inscribed in a circle. Prove that if the centre of the circle is inside the 7-gon, then the sum of angles A1, A2 and A3 is less than 450 degrees.

A game: one gives a digit and the second substitutes it instead of a star in **** - **** = . First gives next digit, and so on 8 times. First wants greatest possible difference, second the least. Prove that 1) the first can ensure difference >= 4000 regardless of second; 2) the second can ensure difference <= 4000 regardless of first.
Let x,y be positive numbers, s = min{x, (y+1/x), 1/y}. What is the greatest possible value of s? To what x and y does it correspond?
Point O inside convex polygon makes isosceles triangle with all pairs of its vertices. Prove that O is the centre of the circumscribed circle.
Is it possible to put numbers 0,1 or 2 in the unit squares of 100x100 grid such that every rectangle 3x4 (and 4x3) would contain three zeros, four ones and five twos?
Let sum of positive numbers x1,...,xn be 1. Let s be the greatest of { x1/(1+x1), x2/(1+x1+x2), ..., xn/(1+x1+...+xn)}. What is the minimal possible s? Which xi achieve it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: expected solutions without calculus (derivatives not in school plans).

rubrics_metrics.description: One-round hockey tournament (each plays each once; winner 2 points, loser 0, draw 1). For any subgroup of teams there exists a team (possibly from the subgroup) that has an odd number of points in games with teams of the subgroup. Prove that there was an even number of participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: 174a
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourteen coins: expert knows coins 1--7 are false (lighter) and 8--14 true. Judge only sure true coins equal weight and false equal weight. With balance scales (no weights), how can expert prove coins 1--7 are false in three weighings?

rubrics_metrics.name: 174b
rubrics_metrics.description: How can he prove that coins 1--7 are false and 8--14 are true in three weighings?
Prove that a 9-digit number containing all decimal digits except zero and not ending with 5 cannot be a perfect square.

Given n points, n > 4. Prove that You can connect them with directed edges (arrows) so that you can reach every point from every other point by passing through one or two arrows. (At most one arrow between ordered pair.)

Given an angle with vertex O and a circle touching its sides at A and B. A ray from A parallel to OB meets circumference at C. Segment OC meets circumference at E. Lines AE and OB meet at K. Prove that |OK| = |KB|.
Real numbers a,b,c satisfy: for all x in [-1,1], |a x^2 + b x + c| <= 1. Prove that for same x, |c x^2 + b x + a| <= 2.

Tennis tournament with 1024 players, single-elimination. Federation assigns numbers by skill. If matches between players whose numbers differ by more than 2 always won by lower-numbered player, what is greatest possible winner number?
Square polynomial f(x)=ax^2+bx+c is such that equation f(x)=x has no real roots. Prove that f(f(x))=x has no real roots either.

rubrics_metrics.name: 181a
rubrics_metrics.description: n squares of infinite grid are painted black. Each move all squares change colour according to majority of itself, its right neighbor, and its upper neighbor. Prove that after finite number of moves all black squares will disappear.

rubrics_metrics.name: 181b
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that disappearance happens no later than on the n-th move.

rubrics_metrics.name: 182a
rubrics_metrics.description: Three similar acute triangles AC1B, BA1C, CB1A built externally on triangle ABC with specified equal-angle correspondences. Prove their circumcircles intersect in one point.

rubrics_metrics.name: 182b
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that lines AA1, BB1, CC1 intersect in the same point.
N men are not acquainted. You need to introduce some of them to some such that all men will have different numbers of acquaintances. Prove this is possible for all N.

rubrics_metrics.name: 184a
rubrics_metrics.description: A knight's (king's?) tour on 8x8 visiting all fields once and returning, trajectory drawn gives closed simple broken line. Give example where king could make 28 steps parallel to board sides only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem mentions 'king' moving visiting all fields once returning to start; parts a,b,c ask extremal counts and total broken line length.

rubrics_metrics.name: 184b
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove he could not make less than 28 such steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: 184c
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the maximal and minimal length of the broken line if the side of a field is 1?
Given triangle with sides a >= b >= c and area 1. Prove that b^2 >= 2.
Given a convex n-gon with pairwise non-parallel sides and a point inside it. Prove that there are not more than n straight lines through that point that halve the area of the n-gon.
Prove that for every positive x1,...,x5 holds inequality: (x1+...+x5)^2 >= 4(x1x2 + x3x4 + x5x1 + x2x3 + x4x5).
Given 4 points in 3D not coplanar. What is the number of parallelepipeds such that each given point is a vertex of each parallelepiped?

rubrics_metrics.name: 189a
rubrics_metrics.description: Given some cards with either -1 or +1 on opposite sides. You may choose triple of cards and ask product of the three. What minimal number of questions allow determining all numbers for 30 cards?

rubrics_metrics.name: 189b
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as above for 31 cards.

rubrics_metrics.name: 189c
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as above for 32 cards.

rubrics_metrics.name: 189d
rubrics_metrics.description: Fifty such cards around circumference; allowed to ask product of three consecutive numbers only. Determine product of all 50 numbers; minimal number of questions?
Among all numbers representable as 36^k - 5^l (k,l natural) find the smallest. Prove minimality.

rubrics_metrics.name: 191a
rubrics_metrics.description: Each side of a convex hexagon is longer than 1. Does it necessarily have a diagonal longer than 2?

rubrics_metrics.name: 191b
rubrics_metrics.description: Each main diagonal of convex hexagon is longer than 2. Does it necessarily have a side longer than 1?

Given two circles with radii R and r touching externally. Consider all trapezoids whose lateral sides touch both circles and whose bases touch different circles. Find the shortest possible lateral side.
Given n unit vectors in plane whose sum length is less than one. Prove you can reorder them so that for every k <= n the length of sum of first k vectors is less than 2.
Find all real a,b,c such that for all real x,y,z the equality |ax+by+cz| + |bx+cy+az| + |cx+ay+bz| = |x|+|y|+|z| holds.
Given square ABCD. Points P and Q on sides AB and BC respectively with BP = BQ. Let H be foot of perpendicular from B to PC. Prove angle DHQ is right.

Given red and blue points some connected by segments. A point is 'exclusive' if its colour differs from the colour of more than half of its connected points. Each move repaint an arbitrary exclusive point. Prove after finite moves no exclusive points remain.
Find all natural n and k such that n^n has k digits and k^k has n digits.
Given points D and E on legs CA and CB of an isosceles right triangle with CD = CE. Perpendiculars from D and C to AE meet hypotenuse AB at K and L. Prove |KL| = |LB|.

rubrics_metrics.name: 199a
rubrics_metrics.description: Game 'cats and rats' on 8x8. First has one rat, second several cats. Moves orthogonally; rat can escape off border. If they coincide rat eaten. Players move in turn; second may move all cats independently. a) With two cats and rat on interior, can cats be placed on border fields so they can catch the rat?

rubrics_metrics.name: 199b
rubrics_metrics.description: With three cats but rat moves twice in first turn, prove that the rat can escape.

rubrics_metrics.name: 200a
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that you can rearrange numbers 1..32 so that for every pair none of the numbers between them equals their arithmetic mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: 200b
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you rearrange numbers 1..100 so that for every pair none of the numbers between them equals their arithmetic mean?
Find all three-digit numbers equal to the arithmetic mean of the six numbers obtained by rearranging its digits.
Given a convex polygon that cannot contain any triangle of area 1 inside it. Prove you can place the polygon inside a triangle of area 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: 203a
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f(x) on [0,1] with f(x) >= 0, f(1)=1 and for all pairs {x1,x2} with x1+x2 in domain, f(x1+x2) >= f(x1) + f(x2). Prove f(x) <= 2x for all x.

rubrics_metrics.name: 203b
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the inequality f(x) <= 1.9x valid (under same conditions)?
Given triangle ABC with area 1. Let A',B',C' be midpoints of BC, CA, AB. What is minimal possible area of intersection of triangles A'B'C' and KLM where K,L,M lie on AB', CA', BC' respectively?

rubrics_metrics.name: 205a
rubrics_metrics.description: Triangle ABC rotated about center of circumscribed circle by angle < 180 to A1B1C1. Intersections of corresponding sides [AB] and [A1B1] = C2, [BC] and [B1C1] = A2, [AC] and [A1C1] = B2. Prove triangle A2B2C2 is similar to ABC.

rubrics_metrics.name: 205b
rubrics_metrics.description: Quadrilateral ABCD rotated about circumcenter to A1B1C1D1. Prove the intersections of corresponding lines are vertices of a parallelogram.
Given triangle ABC area 1. First player picks X on AB, second picks Y on BC, first picks Z on AC. First tries to maximize area of triangle XYZ, second minimize. What area can first ensure and how?
What is the smallest perimeter of a convex 32-gon whose vertices lie on integer lattice points (grid with unit squares)?

rubrics_metrics.name: 208a
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 7x7 grid, mark centers of k points so that no quadruple of marked points are vertices of an axis-parallel rectangle. What is maximal k?

rubrics_metrics.name: 208b
rubrics_metrics.description: Same problem for 13x13 square.
Let B1..B6 be midpoints of diagonals A6A2, A1A3, A2A4, A3A5, A4A6, A5A1 of convex hexagon A1..A6. Prove that if hexagon B1..B6 is convex, its area equals one quarter of the original hexagon.
Prove it is possible to find 2^{n+1} of 2^n-digit numbers containing only digits 1 and 2 such that every two differ in at least 2^{n-1} digits.
Given a finite set of polygons in the plane where every two have a common point. Prove there exists a straight line that crosses all the polygons.
Prove that for all positive numbers a,b,c the inequality a^3 + b^3 + c^3 + 3abc > ab(a+b) + bc(b+c) + ac(a+c) holds.

Three flies crawl along perimeter of triangle ABC so that centroid of their masses is constant. One fly has already passed the entire perimeter. Prove the centroid coincides with centroid of triangle ABC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: triangle centroid = intersection of medians.

rubrics_metrics.description: Several 0s,1s,2s on blackboard. Repeatedly erase a pair of different numbers and replace with the number not equal to either (0 for {1,2}; 1 for {0,2}; 2 for {0,1}). Prove that if one number remains, it does not depend on processing order.

Given horizontal strip and n lines intersecting it; every two intersect inside strip and no triple common point. Consider all monotone rising paths along segments turning at intersections. Prove: a) at least n/2 such disjoint paths exist; b) there is a path with at least n segments; c) there is a path using no more than n/2+1 lines; d) there is a path using all n lines.
For which k is it possible to construct a cube k x k x k of black and white 1x1x1 cubes such that every small cube has same colour as exactly two of its neighbours (neighbour if common face)?
Given polynomial P(x) with a) natural coefficients; b) integer coefficients. Let a_n be sum of digits of P(n). Prove that some number occurs infinitely often in sequence a_1, a_2, ...

World and European champions determined in same round-robin tournament with 20 teams, k of them European. European champion decided by games among those k teams only. What maximal k such that the single European champion can be the single world outsider for: a) hockey (draws allowed)? b) volleyball (no draws)?

rubrics_metrics.name: 219a
rubrics_metrics.description: Given reals a1,a2,b1,b2 and positive p1,p2,q1,q2. In 2x2 table with entries (ai + bj)/(pi + qj), prove there is a saddle point: an entry not less than another in same row and not greater than another in same column.

rubrics_metrics.name: 219b
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalize to nxn: given reals ai, bj and positives pi, qj, table entries (ai + bj)/(pi + qj) has a saddle point (entry not less than any in its row and not greater than any in its column).

There are 50 identical clocks lying on a table. Prove there exists a moment when the sum of distances from table center to ends of minute hands is more than the sum of distances from center to centers of the clocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 221a
rubrics_metrics.description: A row of 1000 numbers. Construct next row where under each number a write natural number indicating how many times a occurs in first line. Repeat to form sequence of rows. Prove some row equals its predecessor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 221b
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the 11th line equals the 12th.

rubrics_metrics.name: 221c
rubrics_metrics.description: Give example of initial line such that the tenth row differs from the eleventh.

rubrics_metrics.name: 222a
rubrics_metrics.description: Given three circles of same radius crossing at one point K. Consider three arcs AK, CK, EK (each arc inside one circle, outside second, on border of third). Prove sum of these arcs is 180 degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 222b
rubrics_metrics.description: If three circles intersect forming a curvilinear triangle BDF, prove sum of arcs AB, CD and EF (with arcs as specified) is 180 degrees.
Natural numbers x1,x2 < 1000. Build sequence x3 = |x1 - x2|; x4 = min{|x1-x2|,|x1-x3|,|x2-x3|}; ... where x_k = min{|xi-xj|; 0<i<j<k}. Prove x21 = 0.
Can you label cube vertices with three-digit binary numbers such that numbers at every pair of adjacent vertices differ in at least two digits?
Given 4 vectors a,b,c,d in plane with a+b+c+d = 0. Prove |a|+|b|+|c|+|d| >= |a+d|+|b+d|+|c+d|.
Given 1976-gon. Midpoints of all sides and diagonals are marked. What is greatest number of marked points lying on one circle?
